A byte-corrupt relationships.json is a real failure mode distinct from a recognised-but-wrong shape, and the contract as written doesn't name it.

Conflating the two under one label could lead an implementer to treat the empirically-true fact as compiler-enforced rather than test-enforced.
still_weak_in_adr015_rewrite.severity: minor -- terminology precision issue, not a factual error; the document elsewhere (ADR-015 prose) correctly explains the test-enforcement mechanism, so the risk is localized to a reader who only skims the SS 7.4 block

unsupported_behavioral_claims_this_pass.location: hld.md ADR-015 (SS4, ~line 445-464) and SS 7.4 adapter contract (~line 725-736)
unsupported_behavioral_claims_this_pass.claim: Schema census: 'a census of all 99 knowledge-graph/{slug}/relationships.json files returns six shapes: type+bare-list (58), type+dict-with-edges (22), non-standard edge-key+bare-list (7), empty relationships (7), non-standard edge-key+dict (3), relationship_type+bare-list (2)'. Later: 'The 7 empty-relationship domains map to EmptyByData, a recorded data gap, never an error.'
unsupported_behavioral_claims_this_pass.finding: The 58/22/7(non-standard-bare-list)/3(non-standard-dict)/2(relationship_type) buckets are all independently reproduced exactly by a from-scratch shape classifier written against every one of the 99 relationships.json files on disk. The 'empty relationships (7)' bucket is FALSE: the 7 domains in it -- agritech, assembly-boot, embedded-firmware-kernel, insurance, mobile-engineering, supply-chain, systems-programming -- are not empty. Each contains a real, non-trivial edge list (54 to 85 edges) using the standard 'type' key, but wrapped in a dict under a 'relationships' key instead of 'edges'. An exhaustive re-scan for genuinely empty (0-edge) relationships.json files across all 99 domains found ZERO. This is a real, previously-unexamined 7th container-key shape, not an empty-data condition.
unsupported_behavioral_claims_this_pass.downstream_impact: This is not a cosmetic mislabel. (1) It falsifies the design rationale sentence that these 7 domains map to EmptyByData -- if the adapter is built exactly as ADR-015 describes, these 7 domains would either be misrouted to EmptyByData despite having real data (silently discarding 54-85 real edges each as if the domain had none) or fail to parse at all. (2) SS 7.4's formal contract explicitly states 'container accepted as bare list OR {"edges": [...]}' -- it does not mention a 'relationships' key at all, so as literally specified the adapter has no parse path for these 7 files; they would fall through to ParseError, not EmptyByData as the ADR claims. (3) The SS 7.4 conformance-test claim 'reading all 99 domains yields parse_success_count > 0 for each of the 6 known shapes' cannot be satisfied for this shape under the contract as written, because the contract does not recognize it.
unsupported_behavioral_claims_this_pass.severity: critical -- a foundational premise for the entire ADR-015 design (the shape census) is wrong for one of its six named buckets, and the error propagates into both the design rationale prose and the formal SS 7.4 contract
unsupported_behavioral_claims_this_pass.recommendation: Correct the taxonomy to seven real shapes: reclassify the 7-domain bucket as 'type + dict-with-relationships-key' (not empty), add {"relationships": [...]} as a third accepted container form in the SS 7.4 contract, and either drop the EmptyByData-mapping sentence or replace it with an accurate description of what (if anything) actually produces EmptyByData -- verification found no domain that does.
